clusters.name: Accounts (identity, auth, profile)
clusters.note: Highest in-degree hub in the graph: accounts/service.py#get_by_username is called from social, statuses, timelines, moderation and lists services (18 incoming reference edges) - this is the de facto identity-resolution seam of the app.

clusters.name: Social graph (follow/block/mute)
clusters.note: social/queries.py is a shared read-only predicate layer consumed by accounts, statuses, timelines, notifications AND lists - it is the most reused cross-cutting module after accounts.service.

clusters.name: Statuses + Timelines (posts and feeds)
clusters.note: statuses/service.py is the largest and highest out-degree module (38 outgoing edges): create/edit/delete/reblog/favourite plus visibility (can_view) which timelines/service.py depends on directly.

clusters.name: Notifications
clusters.note: notify() is called from both social/service.py (follow requests/follows) and statuses/service.py (mentions/reblogs/favourites) - a fan-in point from two other clusters.

clusters.name: Moderation (reports, suspension, roles)
clusters.note: Depends on both accounts.service (role/suspension) and statuses.service (soft_delete on resolve) - a downstream consumer of two clusters, staff-gated via deps.Staff.

clusters.name: Lists (unreferenced from the API surface)
clusters.note: Internally cohesive (service.py calls accounts.service and social.queries correctly, and models.py defines valid SQLAlchemy tables) but NOT wired into minidon/main.py, minidon/models.py, or any other cluster. See orphans below (MW-W01 confirmed).

orphans.notes: Confirms ingestion warning MW-W01. Verified independently via import/call analysis: minidon/main.py imports exactly 6 routers (accounts, social, statuses, timelines, notifications, moderation) and minidon/models.py (the single-import aggregator) imports exactly 5 domain models.py modules - neither includes minidon.lists. grep across the full minidon/ and tests/ trees for the string 'lists' found zero references outside minidon/lists/ itself. The package has no routes.py, so even if it were imported nothing would mount it on the ASGI app. Internally the package is well-formed (List/ListMember models extend Base correctly; service.py's create_list/add_member call into accounts.service and social.queries exactly as other domain services do) - this looks like an incomplete feature, not broken code.

metadata.scope: Single repository (minidon) per millwright.config.yaml; project.repos has one entry (role: backend). No cross-repository edges exist or are expected for this baseline - crossRepoCallPaths is intentionally empty, not unresolved.
coverageNotes: Nodes exist for every module/class/function/method across all 45 parsed Python files (minidon/ + tests/), per ingest-report.json parseResults. Line ranges were derived by direct inspection of the pinned commit e1fbd3a9c8d863086cb9e4005b411d7c33c91488 (read-only; no writes to the source repo, per I-01).

'calls' edges were built from grep-verified call sites for the service/route/query layers (the behaviorally significant layer for capability mapping), plus intra-module private-helper calls (e.g. statuses/service.py's _validate_text, _sync_mentions_and_tags) confirmed by direct source inspection.

'uses' edges cover exception classes, config.Settings, and ORM/Pydantic model classes referenced as types - these are modelled at one representative edge per (consuming module or function) -> (class), not one edge per individual type-annotation occurrence, to keep the graph legible. This is a deliberate granularity choice, not a gap in coverage of which modules use which types.

FastAPI route handlers, FastAPI dependency functions (Depends()), the DomainError exception handler, and pytest fixtures/test functions are invoked by their respective frameworks via decorator metadata or naming convention, never by a literal call expression in source. These are modelled as edges from ext:fastapi / ext:pytest with confidence='dynamic' or 'reflective' so they are not misclassified as unreferenced dead code (57 dynamic + 54 reflective edges).

External dependency nodes were created only for the frameworks named in ingest-report.frameworks (fastapi, sqlalchemy, pydantic, uvicorn, httpx, pytest) plus stdlib enum (for StrEnum inheritance). Other stdlib imports (os, re, hashlib, hmac, secrets, datetime, typing, dataclasses, collections.abc) are omitted as external nodes - they carry no domain-structural meaning for capability mapping - and are instead left as part of each file's recorded imports in ingest-report.json.
